title: 공원 가기
intro: 설문에서 '공원 가기'를 고르면 자주 가는 공원 묘사 → 공원에서 하는 일(루틴) → 공원에서의 기억에 남는 경험 → 어릴 때와 지금의 공원 비교가 자주 출제됩니다. 아파트에서 걸어서 5분 거리의 작은 동네 공원(저녁 산책)과 자전거로 10분 거리의 한강공원(조깅·피크닉) 두 곳으로 모든 답을 연결하세요. 동네·조깅·집 주제와 배경이 겹치므로 같은 묘사를 그대로 재활용할 수 있습니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about that.' 같은 시작 문장 → 공원 위치·모습 → 언제·누구와·무엇을 하는지 → 왜 좋은지(바쁜 일상 속 휴식) → 'Yeah, that's why I love ~.' 마무리 문장.
묘사는 위치(집에서 5분) → 크기 → 보이는 것 3가지(산책로, 벤치, 나무) → 분위기(조용함) 순서로, 쉬운 단어로 짧게 말합니다.
동네 공원은 '저녁 산책, 엄마·남동생 Junho와', 한강공원은 '주 3회 조깅, 친구 Minji와 피크닉'으로 역할을 나눠 고정하세요.
IH 이상은 계절 변화(봄 벚꽃, 가을 단풍), 과거와 비교(used to ~), 감정 표현을 더해 길이를 늘립니다.

expressions.en: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about that.
expressions.ko: 아, 공원이요? 네, 그 얘기 해 드릴게요.
expressions.note: 시작 문장: 질문 키워드를 되받아 말하며 시작하세요.

expressions.en: There's a small park about five minutes from my apartment.
expressions.ko: 저희 아파트에서 5분 정도 거리에 작은 공원이 있어요.
expressions.note: There's ~ near/from …: 장소 묘사의 기본 문장

expressions.en: It has a walking path, some benches, and lots of trees.
expressions.ko: 산책로랑 벤치 몇 개, 그리고 나무가 많이 있어요.

expressions.en: It's really quiet and peaceful, especially in the evening.
I usually take a walk there after dinner.
Sometimes I go with my mom or my brother Junho.
expressions.ko: 가끔 엄마나 남동생 Junho랑 같이 가요.

expressions.en: The Han River park is only ten minutes away by bike.
Walking in the park helps me clear my head.
In spring, the whole path is covered with cherry blossoms.
It's the perfect place to take a break from my busy schedule.
expressions.ko: 바쁜 일정에서 잠깐 쉬기에 딱 좋은 곳이에요.

expressions.en: When I was a kid, I used to play on the swings there for hours.
expressions.ko: 어렸을 때 거기서 몇 시간씩 그네를 타곤 했어요.

expressions.en: We ordered fried chicken and had a picnic by the river.
Yeah, that's why the park is one of my favorite places.
expressions.ko: 네, 그래서 공원이 제가 제일 좋아하는 장소 중 하나예요.
expressions.note: 마무리 문장: 'Yeah, that's why ~'로 이유를 정리하며 끝내세요.

expressions.en: Watching the sunset over the river, I felt like all my stress just melted away.
expressions.ko: 강 위로 지는 노을을 보면서 스트레스가 싹 녹아내리는 것 같았어요.

expressions.en: It's not fancy at all, but it's the place where I feel most like myself.
expressions.ko: 전혀 화려하진 않지만, 제가 가장 저다워지는 곳이에요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like going to parks. Tell me about a park you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
questions.ko: 설문에서 공원에 가는 것을 좋아한다고 하셨습니다. 자주 가는 공원에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 위치(아파트에서 걸어서 5분) → 크기·모습(산책로, 벤치, 나무, 놀이터) → 분위기 → 좋아하는 이유 → 마무리.
보이는 것을 3가지 정도 'There is/are ~'로 나열하면 묘사가 쉽게 완성됩니다.
IH 이상은 계절에 따른 변화(봄 벚꽃, 가을 단풍)와 한강공원 한 문장을 덧붙이세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about that. There's a small park about five minutes from my apartment. It's in a quiet neighborhood. The park has a walking path, some benches, and lots of trees. There's also a small playground for kids. In the evening, it's really quiet and peaceful. I often walk there after dinner. It helps me relax after my busy day at school. Yeah, that's the park I go to the most.
answers.IH: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about that. The park I go to most often is a small neighborhood park near my apartment. It only takes about five minutes to walk there, so it's really convenient. The park isn't very big, but it's really nice. There's a walking path that goes around the park, and there are wooden benches along the path. There are also lots of tall trees and a small playground for kids. In spring, the whole path is covered with cherry blossoms, and in fall, the leaves turn red and yellow. In the evening, it's quiet and peaceful, and I can hear birds. If I want a bigger park, I ride my bike to the Han River park, which is about ten minutes away. Yeah, that's the park I go to the most.
answers.AL: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about that. The park I go to most often is a small neighborhood park just five minutes from my apartment. I've lived in this area for about ten years, so I've basically grown up with this park. It's not big or fancy at all. There's a walking path that loops around the whole park, and it takes about ten minutes to walk one lap. Along the path, there are wooden benches, some exercise machines that older people love, and lots of tall trees that give great shade in summer. In the middle, there's a little playground where kids are always running around after school. What I love most is how it changes with the seasons. In spring, the whole path is covered with cherry blossoms, and in fall, it turns red and gold. In the evening, the streetlights come on and it gets really calm, so it's the perfect place to take a break from my busy schedule. When I want more space, I ride my bike to the Han River park, but this little park still feels like home. So yeah, that's the park I go to the most.

questions.en: What do you usually do when you go to the park? When do you usually go, and who do you go with?
questions.ko: 공원에 가면 보통 무엇을 하나요? 주로 언제 가고, 누구와 함께 가나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제(평일 저녁, 주말) → 누구와(엄마·Junho / 혼자) → 무엇을(산책, 음악, 조깅) → 끝나고 하는 일 → 마무리.
동네 공원(산책)과 한강공원(조깅·주 3회 30분)을 나눠 말하면 내용이 풍부해집니다.
usually, sometimes, once in a while 같은 빈도 표현을 꼭 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about what I do at the park. I usually go to the park near my apartment after dinner. Sometimes I go with my mom, and sometimes I go alone. We walk around the park for about thirty minutes. When I'm alone, I listen to music with my earphones. Three times a week, I also go jogging at the Han River park. After that, I feel really refreshed. Yeah, that's what I usually do at the park.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about what I usually do at the park. On weekdays, I'm pretty busy with classes, so I usually go to the park near my apartment after dinner to take a short walk. Most of the time, I go with my mom. We walk around the park two or three times and talk about our day. Sometimes my brother Junho comes too, but he usually just plays basketball with his friends. When I go alone, I put on my earphones and listen to IU's songs. I also go jogging at the Han River park three times a week. It's about ten minutes away by bike, and I run there for about thirty minutes. After walking or jogging, I sometimes stop by the convenience store for a cold drink. Yeah, that's my usual routine at the park.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about what I usually do at the park, because it's a big part of my daily routine. Since my weekdays are packed with classes, the park is kind of my way to recharge. Most evenings after dinner, I go for a walk at the small park near my apartment, usually with my mom. We walk around the path a few times and chat about everything, from my group projects to what we should have for dinner tomorrow. Honestly, it's one of my favorite parts of the day. My little brother Junho sometimes tags along, but he always ends up playing basketball with his friends instead. When I go by myself, I put on my earphones, listen to IU's ballads, and just clear my head. Three evenings a week, I ride my bike to the Han River park, which is about ten minutes away, and go jogging for about thirty minutes. Running by the river while the sun goes down is the best feeling. On the way back, I usually grab a cold drink at the convenience store. So yeah, that's pretty much what I do at the park, and it really keeps me sane.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a park. When was it, who were you with, what happened, and why do you still remember it?
questions.ko: 공원에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험에 대해 말해 주세요. 언제였고, 누구와 함께였으며, 무슨 일이 있었고, 왜 아직도 기억에 남나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와(지난봄 시험 끝난 날, Minji와 한강공원) → 무슨 일(치킨 배달, 돗자리, 노을) → 예상 못 한 사건(갑자기 비) → 느낌 → 마무리.
과거 시제를 일관되게 쓰고, first, then, suddenly, in the end 로 이야기를 이어 가세요.
IH 이상은 '갑자기 비가 왔다' 같은 작은 반전을 넣으면 이야기가 생생해집니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, let me think. Last spring, I went to the Han River park with my friend Minji. It was right after our midterm exams. We rode our bikes there. We sat on a mat by the river and ordered fried chicken. It was delivered right to the park! We ate, talked, and watched the sunset. It was so beautiful. I felt really happy because I was so stressed before. Yeah, that's my most memorable day at the park.
answers.IH: Oh, let me think. My most memorable experience at a park was last spring at the Han River park. It was the day our midterm exams finished, so my friend Minji and I wanted to celebrate. We rode our bikes there because it's only about ten minutes from my place. We spread a mat on the grass near the river and ordered fried chicken. In Korea, you can get food delivered right to the park, so it was really easy. We ate, talked about our exams, and watched the sunset. But then, suddenly, it started to rain. We grabbed our things and ran under a bridge, laughing the whole time. We were totally wet, but it was so much fun. We waited there and kept talking until the rain stopped. Yeah, that's why I still remember that day.
answers.AL: Oh, let me think. The most memorable experience I've had at a park was last spring at the Han River park with my friend Minji. It was the day our midterms finally ended, and we were both completely exhausted, so we decided to celebrate. We rode our bikes there, which only takes about ten minutes from my apartment, and spread a mat on the grass right by the river. Then we did the most Korean thing ever. We ordered fried chicken and had it delivered straight to the park. We ate, laughed, and complained about our exams for hours. Watching the sunset over the river, I felt like all my stress just melted away. But then, out of nowhere, it started pouring. We had no umbrellas, so we grabbed the leftover chicken and ran under a bridge, screaming and laughing the whole way. By the time we got there, we were soaked from head to toe. We ended up waiting under the bridge for almost an hour, just talking. It wasn't a perfect day, but that's exactly why I remember it so clearly. So yeah, that's my favorite park memory.

questions.en: How are parks today different from the parks you went to when you were a child? What has changed?
questions.ko: 요즘 공원은 어렸을 때 가던 공원과 어떻게 다른가요? 무엇이 바뀌었나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 어렸을 때 공원(놀이터, 모래, 그네) → 지금 공원(산책로, 운동기구, 카페, 깨끗함) → 사람들이 하는 일의 변화 → 내 생각 → 마무리.
'When I was a kid, ~. But these days, ~.' 구조를 반복해 대조를 분명하게 하세요.
AL은 좋아진 점과 아쉬운 점(아이들이 밖에서 덜 논다)을 함께 말해 균형 있게 마무리합니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me compare them. When I was a kid, parks were pretty simple. There was a playground with sand, swings, and a slide. I used to play there with my friends after school. These days, parks are much nicer. They have clean walking paths, exercise machines, and nice benches. There are also more trees and flowers. Many people go to parks to walk or jog now. Yeah, that's how parks have changed.
answers.IH: Okay, let me compare them. When I was a kid, the parks near my home were pretty simple. There was usually a small playground with sand, a slide, and some swings. I used to play there with my friends for hours after school. There weren't many trees, and the benches were old. These days, parks are much nicer and cleaner. The park near my apartment has a smooth walking path, exercise machines, and lots of trees and flowers. The Han River park also has bike paths, convenience stores, and even food trucks. I think people use parks differently now, too. In the past, parks were mostly for kids, but now adults go there to walk, jog, and relax. My mom and I walk there almost every evening. Yeah, that's how parks have changed since I was little.
answers.AL: Okay, let me compare them, because parks have changed a lot since I was little. When I was a kid, the parks in my neighborhood were really basic. There was usually a small playground with sand, a metal slide that got super hot in summer, and a couple of swings. I used to play there with my friends for hours after school until my mom called me home for dinner. There weren't many trees or nice benches, so adults didn't really spend time there. These days, parks are a completely different story. The park near my apartment now has a smooth walking path, exercise machines, and lots of trees and flowers that the city takes care of. The Han River park is even more impressive. It has long bike paths, convenience stores, and food trucks, and you can even get chicken delivered to your mat. I think the biggest change is who uses parks. They used to be mostly for kids, but now people of all ages go there to walk, jog, or just relax. The only sad part is that I don't see as many kids playing outside as before. So yeah, that's how parks have changed.

pronunciation.tip: '파크'가 아니라 입을 크게 벌린 '파-'에 r을 굴려 '파ㄹ크'처럼, 끝 k는 짧게 끊으세요.
walking의 l은 소리 나지 않아요. path의 th는 혀끝을 이 사이에 두고 바람만 내보냅니다.
'벤치'의 끝은 '치'를 길게 하지 말고 /tʃ/로 짧게 끊어 주세요.
blossoms의 'blo'는 '블라'에 가깝고, 끝 s는 z 소리로 울려 줍니다.
첫 음절 'pea'를 길게 강조하고, 뒤 'ful'은 약하게 '펄'로 넘기세요. 끝 l은 혀를 윗잇몸에 붙입니다.
